summary: Gold fell about 8-9% in a week as AI and tech worries triggered broad de-leveraging that dragged liquid assets down. Technicals favour a near-term bounce but the bigger picture is negative because the US dollar looks to have completed a base. Positioning is lower but not yet fully flushed out.
watching: PCE inflation (25 Nov); Fed December hike and size; COMEX positioning; dollar index breaking above its base; support at 3500 then 3450 and 3320

institution: World Gold Council (Gold and AI article)
summary: The direct link between AI and gold is small (technology is only about 6-7% of yearly demand). The bigger effects are indirect: energy and inflation and geopolitics can support gold; productivity-driven higher real rates and extra mining supply can weigh on it.
watching: Real yields; US dollar; investment flows; central bank buying

summary: Cut its gold forecasts to 4150 dollars for 2026 and 4800 dollars for 2027 as the hawkish Fed bites, while keeping a longer-term constructive view.
watching: Fed rate path; central bank buying

summary: Wall Street kept its bearish bias after gold dropped below 3800 dollars. One analyst said the metal could lose another 400-500 dollars before meaningful support, blaming dollar strength, rising rates and liquidation from the tech sell-off.
watching: Chance of a 50 basis point December hike; further tech liquidation

summary: Said the tech sell-off may have caused forced selling of safe-haven assets such as gold, including margin calls, rather than a change in the gold story itself.
watching: Whether the tech sell-off deepens; oil and Strait of Hormuz headlines

summary: A powerful macro-driven dollar rally: short-dated US yields rose about 40 basis points in a week after Fed hike talk. MUFG noted roughly 28 basis points of hikes priced by December and 43 by January.
watching: Short-dated US yields; a big US tech sell-off could pull yields down

institution: Bank of America Global Fund Manager Survey (Nov)
summary: Fund managers cut tech sharply (net overweight fell to 12% from 37%). Cash is about 3.6%, a record 38% say companies are overinvesting, only 3% expect a recession, and 17% see gold as the best asset for 2027. The survey is often used as a contrarian gauge.
watching: AI overinvestment; crowded semiconductor trade; Fed in December

summary: Reported to have gone maximum overweight global stocks, seeing about 15% upside for the S&P 500 on AI capital spending.

The Fed held at 3.75-4.00% with two officials voting for a hike. Waller floated a 50 basis point December hike if inflation ran hot, and minutes showed broad support for tightening. CME FedWatch showed roughly 93% odds of a 25 basis point December hike.
watching: October PCE inflation; size and pace of 2027 hikes in the December guidance

summary: The latest S&P Global PMIs were strong (manufacturing 54.9, services 56.1, composite 55.9) with consensus for the November flash readings near the same levels. Strong growth gives the Fed room to keep tightening, which is a headwind for gold.
watching: Flash PMI for November; prices-paid components

summary: Consumer confidence jumped to 103.3 in November from 91.9, far above forecasts and the highest since January 2025. It adds to the case for tighter policy.
watching: Spending and inflation data; Fed reaction

summary: Calls the fundamental outlook for gold predominantly negative in the short term because of US monetary policy, even though safe-haven demand remains a long-term support.
Reads the gold sell-off as forced cash-raising rather than a verdict on growth: falling bond yields and a steady dollar are what investors do when they want safety.
